name: INDONESIA
lead: Indonesia is the world's biggest archipelago, with over 17,000 islands. It is wider than the USA. Volcanoes rumble under rainforests where orangutans swing through the trees. Ancient temples rise from rice terraces.
geo: Indonesia sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, a ring of volcanoes. It has 130 active volcanoes, more than any other country. Krakatoa's 1883 eruption was heard in Australia, 3,100 km away.
The islands stretch 5,100 km from east to west, about the distance from London to Tehran. Some have jungle mountains. Others are flat coral islands.
animals: Sumatra is the only place where tigers, elephants, rhinos and orangutans share one rainforest. The Komodo dragon grows up to 3 m long and lives on only a few islands.
The Coral Triangle around eastern Indonesia has the richest sea life on Earth. It has 600+ kinds of coral and 3,000 kinds of fish.
culture: Indonesia has 300+ ethnic groups and 700 languages. The national language, Bahasa Indonesia, unites them all at school. Wayang kulit shadow puppet shows can last all night.
Batik is cloth dyed in wax patterns. People wear it at weddings and offices. A gamelan orchestra plays bronze gongs that shimmer like a waterfall of notes.
history: Hindu and Buddhist kingdoms thrived here for a thousand years. Borobudur, a giant temple from around the year 800, is the world's largest Buddhist monument.
The Dutch ruled for three and a half centuries, drawn by nutmeg, pepper and cloves. Leader Sukarno declared independence on 17 August 1945.
wows: Indonesia has about 130 active volcanoes, more than any other country.
The island of Java holds 155 million people, the world's most crowded big island.
Komodo dragons can sense prey with their tongues from up to 9 km away.
Borobudur's 2,672 carved panels, laid end to end, would stretch over 6 km.
Indonesia grows about 75% of the world's nutmeg.
Its 700-year-old motto, 'Bhinneka Tunggal Ika', means Unity in Diversity (many peoples, one nation).
Indonesia is moving its capital to a brand-new jungle city, Nusantara, on Borneo.

myths.fact: Orangutans are apes, not monkeys. They have no tail. Their name means 'person of the forest' in Malay.

myths.myth: Spices were once cheap and common
myths.fact: Nutmeg was so valuable that in 1667 the Dutch swapped Manhattan (now New York) for tiny Run island.
